facts.text: Pearce was founded after James Pearce’s 1894 gold discovery, sparking the Commonwealth Mine that produced over $10 million in precious metals.
The town’s historic jail, built in 1915, features 10‑inch concrete walls and now belongs to the Old Pearce Preservation Association.
Pearce’s elementary school, established in 1912, still stands and is one of the few surviving early 20th‑century school buildings in the valley.
In 1903, a railroad station opened, linking Pearce to regional mining hubs and helping relocate homes from Tombstone.
The Commonwealth Mine produced about $8 million in silver and $2.5 million in gold between 1895 and 1942, making it one of Arizona’s major silver producers.
At 4,400 feet elevation, Pearce enjoys milder summers that support vineyards, earning it recognition as an American Viticultural Area.
